lesson_title: Why Your Green Shirt Turned Black
hook_text: Under a red disco light, your white shirt glows red and your friend's green shirt turns black. Nobody changed clothes. What happened?
clip_script: A school disco, lit by one red spotlight. A white shirt glows red. A green shirt looks black. A blue poster vanishes. Nothing changed but the light. Here is the secret. White light is all the colours mixed. Objects soak up some colours and bounce back others, and the colour you see is the light that bounces back to your eye. A red apple bounces back red. A leaf bounces back green. White paper bounces back everything; black soaks up everything. Now switch to red light. There is only red to bounce back. The white shirt bounces back red, so it looks red. The green shirt can only bounce back green, but there is no green, so it bounces back nothing and looks black. And all that soaked-up light becomes heat, which is why a black car in Upington gets so hot.
visual_style: A whiteboard disco with a red spotlight, then a white light beam hitting an apple with coloured arrows absorbed and a red arrow reflected, then shirts changing colour under red light.
pacing: A punchy opening puzzle, a clear rule, then a satisfying solve.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and predict colours under coloured light.
